item.research_question: How does temperature affect the wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coatings?
item.test_conditions: Temperatures of 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K
key_findings: With the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases
The friction coefficients increased with the temperature, especially when the temperature reached 1200 K
The hardnesses of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating were basically the same at 300 K and 600 K, but decreased significantly at higher temperatures
The elastic modulus increased significantly from 173 GPa to 219 GPa when the temperature increased from 300 K to 600 K
The density of dislocations at 600 K was significantly reduced compared with that at 300 K
The wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating decreases sharply when the temperature reaches 900 K
item.mechanism: The increase in temperature leads to the increase in the proportion of disordered atoms in the material, resulting in a significant decrease in the normal force and friction coefficient
item.limitations: The effect of changes in the proportion of elements in the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy material on wear resistance was not analyzed
item.future_work: Subsequent analysis can be conducted by changing the proportion of elements to obtain the external influencing mechanism, and the influence of roughness on the wear resistance of materials can be studied by changing the surface morphology of the material
quotes: The friction coefficients increased with the temperature, especially when the temperature reached 1200 K

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does temperature affect the wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coatings?. System: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy. Processing: Molecular dynamics simulation. Test conditions: Temperatures of 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K. Findings: With the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases; The friction coefficients increased with the temperature, especially when the temperature reached 1200 K; The hardnesses of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating were basically the same at 300 K and 600 K, but decreased significantly at higher temperatures; The elastic modulus increased significantly from 173 GPa to 219 GPa when the temperature increased from 300 K to 600 K; The density of dislocations at 600 K was significantly reduced compared with that at 300 K; The wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating decreases sharply when the temperature reaches 900 K. Mechanism: The increase in temperature leads to the increase in the proportion of disordered atoms in the material, resulting in a significant decrease in the normal force and friction coefficient. Limitations: The effect of changes in the proportion of elements in the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy material on wear resistance was not analyzed. Future work: Subsequent analysis can be conducted by changing the proportion of elements to obtain the external influencing mechanism, and the influence of roughness on the wear resistance of materials can be studied by changing the surface morphology of the material. Quote: "The friction coefficients increased with the temperature, especially when the temperature reached 1200 K"
